Brief Review

Bruce Willis plays Dr. Paul Kersey who, after the murder of his wife and attempted murder of his daughter decides to take matters into his own hands to seek revenge on those who stole not just his property but the life of his loved one.

A new age spin on the timeless classic revenge story by the same name. Entertaining but this ain’t no Charles Bronson level of revenge.

Story

The movie takes a good 20 minutes to build up to the actual plot of the movie. This time is spent to attempt to get the viewer to feel for and fall in love with the Kersey family. The daughter getting accepted into her college of choice, Paul’s brother a lovable but black sheep of the family, the wife (Lucy) being a loving mother that everyone wishes for, all icons to show how much of a loving and stable family they are.

Another 15 minutes for Paul to experience events that makes him come to the realization that if he wants to protect his family that he needs to protect his whole town, to fix the problems that the police are unable to do. To rid the city of the crime that plagues everyone’s safety.

It is around this point that Paul finally buys a gun and executes the first criminal, which was recorded and uploaded to the internet. Now, Paul is starting to get a fan base but no one knows of his true identity.

What was good

This was a solid revenge story. Well written (except for 2 major gripes I had, explained below), and a great atmosphere. While the emotional scenes were not 100 percent believable, they passed the sniff test. They did a great job of incorporating the internet age and other media to help build up “The Grim Reaper” that Paul got nicknamed. There was no wild fight scenes, unbelievable back and forth, rather this was more of a quick execution style death scenes. Some gun fights, which lasted 2-4 minutes tops instead of the unbelievable 10 minute gun fight with 100 rounds and no reloads, were decently choreographed.

** What was bad**

There were three things that made me give the score a 7 instead of a 9, and these had to do with specific scenes and how they were done. So, if you don’t want spoilers, watch the movie and then come back (one of them deals with the ending).

1) I have luck in a fight scene. Nothing I hate more than the hero winning a fight because of some dumb luck. In one scene, Paul enters a bar who’s owner had the items that were stolen from him. So, he went to get his stuff back. While there, someone came in to help the owner and got into a fight with Paul. Paul lost the fight and got knocked back against the wall. He hit the wall so hard that on the shelf above him was a bowling ball, which fell off it’s stand and rolled off the shelf hitting the attacker on the head, saving Paul’s life. That is shit writing and ruined a good portion of the vibe of the movie.

2) The stupid table with the button on the side that lowers a shelf to give access to a hidden firearm. There was a commercial early on in the movie showing it off that the local gun store had. Seeing the commercial was such blatant foreshadowing (especially for anyone who has seen the trailer because the scene they showed in the trailer was at the end of the movie). And this is why I hated this. Not only because of the blatantly obvious foreshadowing, which I hate, but at the end of the movie when Paul used the table to get his rifle to kill the person in the doorway… It’s his house, his special basement room, it would have been more believable if he had a hand gun hidden between the cushions or behind the couch. It’s like this table was included into the movie because the writers thought it would look cool. It didn’t. It stood out like a sore thumb.

3) And speaking of the story, Bethany (the cute little blonde that was helping Paul with his first purchase) was portrayed as a bubble, extra friendly sales person. She stood out entirely from the movie, like she was out of place there. And her acting was way over the top for what was supposed to be a typical sales person.

Because of those three things, I had to knock my score down because they ruined the flow of the movie.

** Final Thoughts**

The Death Wish remake was a decent movie, more than mildly entertaining, and typical of a revenge movie. If you are a fan of revenge movies, might as well buy it. If you are a fan of Bruce Willis, it’s worth a watch. If you were expecting Charles Bronson, not worth your time.

But he turns out more than his shares of stinkers so really that this film is even watchable is a credit to the director Eli Roth, who I think is underappreciated.
